## Chapter Eleven

Factory Reset





The big car landed in the back of a four-story brick federalist style house. Landing in the shade Lucas looked up without the sun in his eyes and appraised the stately property. “I guess this guy has some money” Lucas stated, only then realizing how lame it was for an ex con to talk about a rich patron. Jesus, he thought, sounds like I want to rob the place and he chuckled getting a curious look from Job. Lucas waved him off and they both walked to the back door. Lucas looked around the large property, he didn’t know the doctor hell he barely knew Job, and now he was putting his life in freedom in their hands he thought, thought Job had kept him out of jail this long and a lot had gone into getting him out, but why, sighing he knew only Dyson had the answer to those questions. They walked into the door and came into a large kitchen, white tile and light wood filled the room.



Standing in the center of the bright room was a small pudgy bespectacled man of Indian descent. The smile on his face was genuine when he spied Job. “its good to see you my friend” the doctor said to the large bear of a man, his Indian accent heavy but his words still understandable. “Hello, my friend, it has been too long” the small doctor said, his grin spreading across his entire face as he looked his friend over. Job just nodded “far too long, thank you for doing this, Eagle thanks you personally” he said causing Lucas to cock his head, he had not heard this name, at least he thought it was a name, unless there was some unnamed bird out there everyone was deferring to. Job looked over at Lucas and the look told him to be silent, so he did, instead opting to concentrate on the kitchen, he had never seen one so big before. Something was out of place and he couldn’t quite put his finger on it.



It was a kitchen, looked like most kitchens he had seen, except the equipment in it was much nicer than anything he or his friends had, then it hit him. All the appliances were old, or old school he thought cribbing the term from his father, none of them had touch screens or electronics of any kind, in fact when he looked around the whole kitchen, there were no speakers or sensors like you would find in any home, every house was built now a days with entire smart home architecture, built in cameras, speakers, sensors so that whichever software you used could see, hear and respond to you no matter where you were in the house.



He thought that odd and filed it away for later. The doctor interrupted his thoughts, motioning Lucas to follow him. Looking at Job worriedly, the old man nodded smiling and took a seat at the kitchen’s center island. “You will be fine, go with doc, he will fix you up” he said settling in.



Lucas made his way down the wood lined hallway and through a small door into what looked like a guest bedroom that had been outfitted with the latest in surgery appliances.



The doctor walked over to a small table and began to turn on equipment as he sat on the small rolling stool. “Our goal is, to alter your face to not be recognizable as yourself, we will do this by altering your cheeks, your dental bite, your eye color and your facial profile by changing your nose and the angle of your forehead and then we will finish out by changing your jawline and your chin” he said concentrating on the screens as the equipment came online.



He switched on the holo table and a three-dimensional depiction of Lucas floated there. The doctor spent a few moments concentrating on it and as Lucas watched, he began to reach out and touch points on the holo picture. As he did the picture’s facial features began to morph and distort. Lucas watched in awe as the face that had once floated above the table changed in small but meaningful ways.



He could tell at the core it was still him, but enough on the face had changed that he didn’t even think anyone would be able to recognize him.



Clearing his throat, he pulled the doctor from his concentration. “yes” he said half distracted and Lucas stepped closer “Um, you have me with two eyes sir” he said and slowly removed the bandages on his face, showing the doctor the closed socket.



Shaking his head, the small man walked over and gently but expertly prodded at the sutured wound “Damn butchers” he hissed disgustedly and withdrew back to the table. “Do not worry, you will have two eyes, I have access to a few very nice appliances, it will take some getting used to but you will be able to see normally when we are done young man” he said with enough conviction that Lucas let out a breath, he had resigned himself to never see out of his right eye again. He said a small prayer and as the doctor motioned him, Lucas laid down on the metal table suddenly feeling nervous. He looked over at the new face that floated above the table, how different it looked, but still enough of the same that he could see himself in it.



The doctor began to collect tools out of a drawer and laying them on a small table, as he did he explained in detail every tool and what it would do , funny enough, it relaxed Lucas, he felt better with this stranger, this small man, displaying his knowledge of his craft.



Once the small tray was setup, the doctor walked over to a small 3d printer on the wall and turned it on. The printer instantly went to work, Lucas couldn’t make out what it was doing but the doctor again was there with his expert knowledge ,as he laid the young man he spoke softly “The printer is printing extensions, in order to change your facial profile , we will add to your bone structure, these appliances will not only change your face, but your bone structure, thus, making it impossible for any facial system to recognize you, you will be under for the procedure and when you wake, you will be swathed in bandages, it will take a few days to recover, for which time you will remain in my care young man” he said in a paternal tone that again comforted Lucas. The man was easy to trust, easy to like, and when he quietly injected him with Demerol, Lucas drifted off, knowing he was in good hands.



Lucas slowly woke, opening his eye he quickly shut it as the sun coming in through the window shone directly in his face. It took him a moment of slowly opening the eye to get used to the bright mid day sun when he did, he found himself no longer In the surgery room, but in what looked like a guest room in the house, the walls were a warm blue lined with expensive cherry furniture. On the far wall was a hutch with a mirror that filled almost the entire wall. Lucas tried to lift himself, to see if he could get a look at his face but it wasn’t at the right angle, and moving too much caused dizziness and pain.



He laid down, realizing the effort had damn near exhausted him. He brought up his hand and gingerly touched at the bandages on his face. Except for the area around his good eye, his face was completely covered. “Don’t play with those” came the friendly but chiding voice of the doctor and Lucas slowly turned his head to see the portly man entering, Job close behind. Lucas could smell chicken broth and realized he was ravenous.



As the doctor approached his stomach grumbled as be brought the soup close to the bed. The doctor smiled laying the bowl down on the cherry table next to the queen size bed. “That is a very good sign” he stated, beginning to poke and prod around Lucas’s neck and face. Never touching hard enough to cause pain and except for a little light pressure, Lucas couldn’t tell he had touched him at all.



The doctor looked over at Job and nodded smiling. The big man let out a relieved sigh. Lucas shot him a curious look “Was there some doubt?” he asked, mildly concerned. Eliciting an apologetic look from the big man. “Sometimes there is some prosthetic rejection from the appliances that went over areas of your skull, but the doc thinks they are good” he said patting Lucas on the arm.



“You should be okay, the worst is over, after the first twenty four hours I could tell they had taken, now that its been forty eight, you appear to be out of the woods.” He said, taking a few syringes and injecting them into an IV bag Lucas had missed, as it hung over the headboard of the cherry wood head board. “whats that” he asked a little alarmed at the sight of so many needles. The doctor smiled reassuringly “Just antibiotics, some pain meds and something to help the appliances take” he answered and then got up, making way for Job to sit, the big man hefted his weight onto the edge of the bed, lowering one side of it. He then gingerly picked up the bowl of soup and began spooning it into Lucas’s mouth. “How long do I have to be like this?” He asked in between mouthfuls of the much-needed broth.



The doctor thought for a moment and then turned towards the dresser, putting away the needles and other small took he had out “Another week and you will be good to move on” he said. “Do not worry, I live alone and no one comes to visit me, I am retired so I will not be missed nor will anyone question why I am home so long” he said as if this would have been Lucas’s next question, it should have been and he chided himself, Dyson had trained him better than that. So, Lucas just nodded as if it would have been the next question and went back to eating soup.



This was his entire week, twice a day the doctor and Job would come in, the doctor would check him and pronounce that he was healing marvelously and then Job would feed him broth and talk to him until the drugs took effect.



On the Seventh day the routine changed, as the doctor entered the room, he proudly announced the bandages would come off today. A very nervous Lucas waited patiently as he felt the small scissors making their way through the ample bandages. He felt a small fluttering in the pit of his stomach and couldn’t decide if it was nervousness or excitement he was feeling. The doctor, lucas realizing he still didn’t know the man’s name and thought randomly if that was because he was rude, or operational security after a moment he thought the latter. The doctor gently lifted off the large amount of gauze surrounding his face and then began to survey his work, running his fingers over the skin, Lucas could feel the light touch, and the twitching of the muscles caused the old Indian to smile “good sign” his thickly accented English sounded more like ‘gud scene’. But Lucas didn’t smile, the fluttering in his stomach was getting worse, as he closely watched the doctors face for any sign of worry or concern. But the doctor was either a true professional or a hell of a poker player. After a maddening thirty minutes, he announced the surgery was a success and brought up a mirror for Lucas to view the old man’s work.



Lucas looked at his swollen mug and winced when finally got a good view of it in the small mirror, it looked like a gorilla had pummeled him something fierce. “The swelling will go down, but the appliances took nicely and the eye looks like it did as well, now I have not turned it on or synced it so you will not see out of it until I do, a few more days and you will be up and around” the doctor soothed , seeing the worried expression on Lucas’s face. He tried to see the face under the swelling but couldn’t really make it out, his cheecks were puffed out and it looked like he had gotten stung by a hundred bees. He put the mirror down and settled back into the bed.



His skin was hot and uncomfortable, but he was glad to be free of the bandages. The doctor, patting the young man on the shoulder, injected the IV bag with more of the drugs, Lucas slowly descending into darkness.



He awoke with a start as the Doctor and Job stood at the foot of his bed arguing, Lucas was still groggy and could only make out a few phrases of the conversation as he shook his head , trying to clear it “…They found out, how did they find out” “…They will be here soon, we have to move him” 
“…He is not ready, you could endanger his recovery”. He finally had cleared enough of the cobwebs from his mind to sit up, at first, he was light headed, but forced himself further upright until he was sitting. “What’s going on” he asked groggily, both men turning to him. Even through the fuzz of the post drug sleep, he could see the worried expression on Job’s face. “We have to get ready to go, someone tipped off the vipers, they are coming here” he said beginning to lift Lucas from the bed “what the hell are vipers?” Lucas asked. As Job lifted him to his feet and began to reach into the dresser, pulling out clothes for him to wear. “Department of Security Secret Police, these are not the guys you want coming for you, they show up and people disappear, we have to go” he said, never once looking up at Lucas.



He helped him dress even as the doctor protested and pushing the old Indian man gently out of the way, Job helped his friend down the stairs and back into the kitchen. He left Lucas leaning up against the center island and went outside, he was back in moments with a large suitcase. “Doc, im sorry” he said and then pulling what looked like a screwdriver handle, pointed it at the doctor, a small red light appeared on the surprised doctor’s forehead and in a moment there was a pinsize smoking hole , and the doctor fell backwards onto the floor dead. “What the hell” Lucas yelled alarmed as he looked between the doctor and Job. “Why did you kill him?” he said, trying to back away from the man who had been so nice to him. Job grabbed him on the arm and brought him closer, his easy manner and smiling face gone, replaced by a much harder appearance. “The doctor knew too much , they would have questioned him” he said , letting Lucas go and putting the large bag on the table, opening it Lucas could see large glass containers and wires leading to a small metal box “What the fuck” he whispered, as Job entered something on the keypad and they both watched as the liquid in the containers began to bubble. “We are leaving NOW” Job said, grabbing Lucas and dragging him out the back door. He all but threw him into the front seat of the black sedan and then got in himself, he lifted off and sped towards the skyway, Lucas looking back watching the house as it grew smaller and smaller. Before they had reached the entrance to the sky way, the house disappeared in a large blossom of blue flame, as debris erupted from the epicenter and once it had cleared, a large hole now resided where once a house, and a nice old man resided.

Lucas could see the Black SUV’s floating down from another direction, people the size of ants tore out of the vehicles and began to encircle the property. “We were lucky, we got enough warning to get out of there, from what I was able to find out, they didn’t know who was there, only that it was a high value target, so with no trace left of any DNA or fluids they could use to match to you, we are good” Job said, Lucas not sure if he was trying to convince himself or Lucas. “Why did you have to kill him, why couldn’t he come with us?” Lucas asked the man, whom he know realized he really didn’t know.



Job entered the skyway and put on the auto drive. Turning to his companion Lucas could see the hard face and calculating eyes, how had he not seen this before that moment he wondered. Amazed at the change in the man. “That man, that nice Indian doctor, used to kill patients for money, rich executives would bring their mistresses or accidents to him, they would go under the pretense of a OBGYN visit to find out the sex of the baby they carried and for a little money, they would never get up from the table, that is how he afforded that big house” Job said, his words a bitter hateful stream.



Lucas wasn’t sure what to think, he had seemed so nice, had taken excellent care of Lucas and had seemed a gentle soul. Could Job be right, or was he telling him this to make him accept his actions. He decided either way, there was no good in arguing with the guy who could kill you as quickly as look at you. They drove on in silence for two hours.



As they rode in silence Lucas kept his eyes below on the scenery doing anything to avoid looking at that hard face that replaced the happy go lucky guy he thought he knew. Then he began to recognize buildings and parks as they drove on high above the earth. As he continued to watch it dawned on him, they were going through Northern Virginia and as he continued to watch, the profile of the Capital and the Washington Monument could be seen in the distance. But before they entered Washington proper, the city passed them on the left as they continued to head north, another city profile emerging from the skyline. Squinting he finally asked “Baltimore?” to Job, who nodded, his face softer than earlier, but still far from the happy old guy who had drove him out of Richmond.



Lucas concentrated on the scenery as the skyline of Baltimore approached quickly.  Within an hour the large Sheraton sign passed by Lucas’s window as the car landed in the carport behind the large hotel, giving him a view of the inner harbor as the sun was setting over the water. Lucas waited in the car as Job secured there rooms. He entered in the back door, Job carrying two pieces of luggage, both seemed heavy by the grunting the old man was exhibiting as they made there way to the elevator.



Within a few minutes, Lucas found himself in a large suite with two king size beds and a great view of the skyline. He walked over and looked out the window, mostly to avoid looking at his companion. He still didn’t know if what he had said about the doctor was true or not and Lucas was conflicted, this man had saved his life and protected him since Richmond, didn’t he owe him the benefit of the doubt, but then again what had Dyson said “trust no one” he could hear from within his memory. “A good operative never trusts anyone, and always verifies that which is told to him” nodding he resolved to keep an open mind, but a cautious one. “What’s Eagle?” he finally asked remembering the conversation he had with the doctor when they had arrived. This seem to surprise Job who stopped unpacking for a moment and looked at him. Finally, a smile spread across his face. “I keep forgetting you don’t know his code name, Its Dyson, though we never use his name, no one but a few know the name Dyson, most know him as Eagle or Prime” he said sitting on the bed and moving the suitcase onto the floor with an unceremonious thump.



Job leaned back, stretching his back and wincing , finally he looked at Lucas “Dyson heads a resistance of sorts, he believes we have a right to fight the government and return this country to its democratic roots, the group spreads far and wide, but its divided into cells, no one knows anyone else, and most of all , no one knows who leads it, Dyson has been at it for nearly twenty years, and I have been fighting alongside of him for fifteen of that.” He said Lucas sitting next to him on the other bed. He remembered Dyson saying something like that and he remembered his statement “If they knew who they had, they would summarily execute me” Lucas sat back and regarded the other man. “Can you tell me about it, obviously I am involved now” Lucas said, hoping the admission to comradeship would loosen Job’s lips. Job looked at him, and those new cold eyes stared into his for almost a minute before he started speaking. “Dyson worked for Department of Security, the right hand of Margaret McDermott, granddaughter of the founder Bruce McDermott, of course his name wasn’t Dyson and like you he had a different face, but it was rumored that he and her, were close and Dyson knew where all the bodies were buried” He started, shifting his position, he eyes moving to the wall to stare into space as if trying to remember. “He led a charmed life, some say a blessed one, there was no one higher in rank or knowledge in DOS then Dyson himself, except for McDermott, but even she deferred to his expertise. Then something happened, one day he gained access to the black archive” Lucas stopped him looking confused “What is the black archive?” he queried to him it sounded like some sort of sacrosanct religious thing, but Job’s face remained serious. “The archive is the true history, it was sealed after the bio-plague, whatever was in it, whatever Dyson saw, changed him”. Job paused again collecting his words.



“No, not changed, opened his eyes” Job corrected, nodding at the word use “that’s more what it was, he learned something and whatever it was changed who he was, from that day he began to collect allies and information” he paused glancing over at Lucas whose attention remained rapt. Leaning over he continued “You see, the new government , the government that we currently live under, was not always the way it was, for all its faults, people had choices, they had decisions, they were the masters of their own destiny” he said trying to convey his feelings to the younger man. Recognizing the look of confusion on his face he shook his head. “One day maybe I’ll explain, but just know there might have been problems, but for the people it was still better than what it became later” he finished, waving his hand as if dismissing his tangent. “Anyway” he continued getting back to his story. “Dyson recognized the problem with resisting the government, he studied all previous attempts to circumvent them, to infiltrate them” he said, a smile cresting his features as if remembering a pleasant memory, but Lucas didn’t want to intrude, this was more information than he had ever gleaned off of Dyson himself. “Everyone is tracked, cameras, your internal sensor” he said pointing to the cuff still on Lucas’s arm. “Hell even guns, everyone that is owned is genetically locked and recorded so if ever used would automatically lead back to the owner, they were very smart and learned quickly over the years, unlike previous autocracies and dictatorships, we now have the technology to truly know what ever man, woman and child in this country is doing” he said.



The thought started Lucas he had never considered it that way, he had always felt safe knowing everything was watched, no crime because the authorities watched every street corner, every camera and before it could go too far, they were always there. But now the more he thought about it the more he could see how something like that could also allow those with agenda to stop anyone who would try to counter them. Lucas never questioned why they were there, they had always just been there, they were convenient, the phones and holo tablets even the cars, all were instruments of surveillance under the guise of convenience he thought, finally understanding what this man meant. “We never gave up our freedom, we just demanded more convenience in our world and they delivered , but at the same time , by doing that and by not questioning it, they were able to also include everything they would need to lay a framework of surveillance into our society, in fact we are our own spies” Lucas whispered, following the thought. Job nodded excitedly “Dyson said you were smart” he said, the pride resounding in his words. “But see its more than that, there is so much to watch, people can’t even hope to keep up, so that was Dyson’s greatest failure wrapped into his most ambitious success” Job said, eliciting an odd curious look from the young man “What the hell is that supposed to mean?” Lucas asked. Not really following him.



“Dyson, wasn’t only the number two in security, he was a brilliant systems designer and programmer, he created a system called Cerberus, it’s an advanced Artificial Intelligent Data Mining Interface, it can see everything , it can collate data at incredible speeds, its ability to reach conclusions based on seemingly random data borders on the supernatural. Once Cerberus went live, six thousand people were rounded up and executed for unpatriotic intent” he said the last words spit from his lips, full of bile. “Until we can defeat that system, we are in the shadows, all we can do is manipulate from the shadows, if we tried to kill everyone in power, it would just transfer to those who could be worse, with access to those same tools.” He said, his words bitter. He got up stretching his legs and Lucas stared at the old man’s silhouette as he stood before the window, staring at the water of the inner harbor. Without turning he finished his story. “One day we will find a way to bring down the system that we allowed to be put in place, and that day, we will be about to root out the leaders who sought to put a yoke on this country not for idealism or something better, but simply for a better bottom line”.



Shrugging Job went silent and walked over to the bed. Lucas had so many questions and for every question two more spawned, the problem is he thought, I don’t understand the questions to ask. Laying down on the bed he lay there recalling the entire conversation. How had he not seen that, he had always loved his phone, his ability to use interactive maps, his ability to video. Chat and take pictures, the safety he felt walking down the street at the sight of a camera, knowing he was watched and protected. Now those same devices could lead to his death, they no longer felt like safe benign objects, but like gargoyles squatting and watching, the second they recognize prey, they would swoop in and attack.



He finally fell asleep around one in the morning listening to the snoring of Job in the next bed.
